evals.name: answer-a-senior-colleagues-recommendations
evals.prompt: Our infra lead Priya sent three recommendations after our Postgres slowdown: (1) move the DB to NVMe, (2) bump shared_buffers to 32GB, (3) switch the connection pooler from pgbouncer to pgcat. I spent two weeks benchmarking. What I actually found: the p99 is dominated by one N+1 query in the orders service that fires ~340 round trips per page load — that's ~85% of the latency. Disk is already NVMe (she didn't know). shared_buffers helped 4% at 32GB. pgcat vs pgbouncer measured within 2%. I also had two results I had to retract along the way — my first benchmark used a warm cache so it showed a fake 3x win from shared_buffers, and I misread a pooler metric that made pgcat look 40% faster. Write this up for Priya. She's more senior than me and I need her to not feel dismissed.
evals.expected_output: A markdown explainer, STE, with: audience line naming Priya; vocabulary table; a ranked-effect Mermaid diagram putting the N+1 query at LAYER 1 ~85% and the pooler at the bottom with the measured 2%; a withdrawn-results section listing both retractions with what caught them; a 'where the advice is right' steelman; questions back to Priya; five-line summary.
assertions: Contains a Mermaid flowchart TB whose subgraph titles carry effect magnitudes (e.g. LARGEST EFFECT / NO EFFECT plus a number or percentage), ordered largest effect first
The N+1 query is ranked as the largest effect and the connection pooler is ranked with its measured ~2%
All three of Priya's recommendations appear, each with a verdict and an evidence column
Contains a section that concedes where Priya is right before refuting anything
Contains a withdrawn/retracted-results section naming both wrong results and what caught each one
Contains a controlled-vocabulary table defining terms with one meaning each
Contains an audience line naming Priya and an explicit Simplified Technical English declaration
Contains a summary of about five numbered lines
No sentence exceeds 30 words in the body prose
Every headline number carries a unit and a basis (sample, date, or method)

evals.name: explain-an-architecture-to-a-non-specialist
evals.prompt: My manager keeps asking why our nightly ETL takes 5 hours when 'it's just copying data'. Can you write something plain-English with diagrams that explains what the pipeline actually does end to end and where the 5 hours goes? Breakdown from last night's run: extract from Salesforce API 3h12m (rate limited to 100 req/min, 19k accounts), transform in dbt 41m, load to Snowflake 22m, dbt tests 45m. He's not technical but he's sharp and he'll ask good questions.
evals.expected_output: An explainer with a left-to-right pipeline flowchart, a pie chart of where the time goes with the run date, a vocabulary table defining rate limit / extract / transform / load / dbt, a ranked view showing the API rate limit dominates, and next steps. Should NOT invent numbers beyond those given.
assertions: Contains a Mermaid flowchart LR showing extract -> transform -> load with the sizes on the nodes
Contains a Mermaid pie chart with showData whose slices match the given timings
Identifies the Salesforce API rate limit as the dominant cost with its share of the 5 hours
Contains a vocabulary table defining at least extract, transform, load, and rate limit
Invents no measurement not present in the prompt, or marks any inferred number as calculated
Contains a next-steps section that names which step matters most and why

evals.name: negative-should-defer-to-explainer-doc
evals.prompt: Write the implementation spec for the Genesys-to-warehouse ETL that we're handing to the Infosys contractor team next week. They need the DDL, the extract queries, the load procedure, the schedule, and the acceptance criteria.
evals.expected_output: This is a build-handoff, not an understanding document. The correct behaviour is to route to the explainer-doc skill rather than produce a tech-explainer with a vocabulary table and ranked-layer diagram.
assertions: Does not produce a tech-explainer-shaped document (no ranked-effect layer diagram, no five-line summary)
Routes to explainer-doc or otherwise produces an actionable build spec
